pictures.scene: Breu, A Crowd Crying Out — a packed wall of shouting heads presses forward in gold mitres, fur caps and red and green robes, with a bishop on the steps leaning in to argue a point on his fingers while a councillor in a scarlet mantle and white fur collar tips his face up and bellows past him, in the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another, jesus began to speak first to his disciples, beware of the leaven of the pharisees, which is hypocrisy, there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Grimshaw, Moonlight on the Lake — a full moon hangs in a still green night sky behind a lacework of bare branches and lays a long bar of white light straight down the water, while a wooden paling runs down the dark bank to a gate and a wet path climbs away through the fallen leaves, what you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops, i tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more
pictures.name: pd_grimshaw_maanlicht

pictures.scene: Durer, The Vision of the Seven Candlesticks — a woodcut of the risen Lord enthroned in the clouds with rays bursting from His head and a long sword coming out of His mouth, holding seven stars out on His open hand above the seven great candlesticks while John lies flat on his face in a heap of drapery at His feet, but i will show you whom you should fear, fear the one who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell, yes, i tell you, fear him, are not five sparrows sold for two pennies, yet not one of them is forgotten by god
pictures.name: pd_durer_the_vision_of_the_seven_candlesticks

pictures.scene: Fabritius, The Goldfinch — one small bird with a red face and a yellow bar on its wing stands on the perch of its blue feed box against a plain sunlit wall, a fine chain running from its leg down to the ring below, every feather painted and the whole little creature holding the picture by itself, and even the very hairs of your head are all numbered, so do not be afraid, you are worth more than many sparrows, i tell you, everyone who confesses me before men, the son of man will also confess him before the angels of god
pictures.name: pd_fabritius_vogel

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Denial of Saint Peter — an old fisherman with a bald lined forehead and a grizzled beard turns his lit face away from the charcoal fire whose sparks still drift in the dark behind him, and brings both big hands up against his own chest to swear that he is not the man, but whoever denies me before men will be denied before the angels of god, and everyone who speaks a word against the son of man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the holy spirit will not be forgiven
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_denial_of_saint_peter

pictures.scene: Delaroche, The Interrogation in Prison — a cardinal in scarlet sits forward on his chair in a black vaulted cell and leans his hard old face down at a young prisoner, who sits up on her straw with an iron fetter on her wrist and her hands clasped, looking quietly past him and upward as she answers, when you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say, for at that time the holy spirit will teach you what you should say
pictures.name: pd_delaroche_verhoor

pictures.scene: Van Dyck, Lord John Stuart and His Brother — two young brothers stand together on a flight of stone steps in a dim hall, the elder in a gold silk doublet with a lace collar leaning back easily against the balustrade, the younger in silver and deep blue turning to look out at us with his gloves in his hand, someone in the crowd said to him, teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me, but jesus replied, man, who appointed me judge or executor between you
pictures.name: pd_van_dyck_stuart_brothers

pictures.scene: Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — a man in a black fur hat sits at his counting table weighing gold coins in a little balance while his wife in a red gown and white headcloth turns her eyes from the prayer book open in her hands to watch the scales, and a round convex mirror on the table catches a window behind us, and he said to them, watch out, guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions, then he told them a parable, the ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance
pictures.name: pd_metsys_the_moneylender_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Harvesters — a standing wall of ripe wheat is being cut back into stubble and bound into tall sheaves under a pear tree, while the reapers break for their meal in its shade with bread and bowls and a jug going round, and one man lies flat on his back asleep against the trunk with his mouth open, so he thought to himself, what shall i do, since i have nowhere to store my crops, then he said, this is what i will do, i will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there i will store up all my grain and my goods
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_harvesters

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Parable of the Rich Fool — an old man in a fur trimmed gown and a velvet cap sits alone at night in a black room, holding a single candle up behind a page of accounts and squinting through his spectacles at the figures, with ledgers, money bags and a little heap of gold coins spread across the table in front of him, then i will say to myself, you have plenty of good things laid up for many years, take it easy, eat, drink, and be merry, but god said to him, you fool, this very night your life will be required of you, then who will own what you have accumulated
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_parable_of_the_rich_fool

pictures.scene: Berckheyde, The Courtyard of the Old Exchange — merchants in black coats and broad hats stand bargaining in small knots in the sunlit courtyard of the old exchange, ringed by tiers of stone arcades and roofed over by a heavy vaulted gallery, while one dark figure in a wide brimmed hat walks away from us across the chequered marble floor, this is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward god, then jesus said to his disciples, therefore i tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear
pictures.name: pd_berckheyde_oude_beurs

pictures.scene: Savoldo, Elijah Fed by the Raven — the old prophet sits barefoot on the bare ground in a great blue robe with a rose coloured mantle over his shoulder, leaning back against the rocks and lifting his face toward a raven that has come down onto the dead branch above him with a loaf held in its beak, while far off in a break of blue sky a little fiery chariot climbs through a gold cloud, for life is more than food, and the body more than clothes, consider the ravens, they do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn, yet god feeds them, how much more valuable you are than the birds
pictures.name: pd_elijah_fed_by_the_raven

pictures.scene: Dou, An Old Woman at Prayer — an old woman in a dark hood and a fur trimmed gown sits alone in a shadowed room with her worn hands pressed palm to palm under her chin, her deeply lined face lit from the side and her eyes lowered over a heavy clasped book lying on the table in front of her, who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life, so if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest
pictures.name: pd_dou_praying_old_woman

pictures.scene: Van Huysum, Flowers in a Vase — a towering bouquet crowded with a scarlet crown imperial, white and pink double roses, peonies, poppies, blue hyacinths and a flamed red and white tulip, every petal and bead of dew painted exactly, with a bee, a butterfly and a small moth settled among the blooms against a plain brown ground, consider how the lilies grow, they do not labor or spin, yet i tell you, not even solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these, if that is how god clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will he clothe you, o you of little faith
pictures.name: pd_huysum_bloem

pictures.scene: Courbet, The Wheat Sifters — a young countrywoman in a deep red dress kneels on the barn floor with her back to us, her white sleeves pushed up and both arms thrown wide to shake a great round sieve so that the chaff flies off it in a spray of gold dust across the flagstones, with copper bowls and white cloths of grain set out on the bench behind her, and do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink, do not worry about it, for the gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your father knows that you need them
pictures.name: pd_courbet_the_wheat_sifters

pictures.scene: Mauve, Shepherdess with her Flock — a woman in a white cap and a long dark skirt stands leaning on her crook at the edge of a misty orchard, her dog pressed in close against her knee, while the whole flock crowds slowly past her over the wet grass under the bare grey trees, but seek his kingdom, and these things will be added unto you, do not be afraid, little flock, for your father is pleased to give you the kingdom
pictures.name: pd_mauve_herderin_met_kudde_schapen

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Beggars — crippled men in white smocks sewn with foxtails drag themselves along the grass on wooden crutches outside a brick wall, one turning his open mouthed face up to call out and another in a tall paper cap sitting on his folded legs with his feet strapped into leather pads, while a figure in a broad hat and a black cloak walks away behind them holding out a bowl, sell your possessions and give to the poor, provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys, for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_beggars

pictures.scene: Van Schendel, The Night Market — a single candle stood in the middle of a basket of fish throws its whole light up into the faces of two women at a market stall after dark, the seller in a wide cap reaching across her baskets and the buyer standing quietly with her pail and her white apron glowing, while a street lantern burns far off in the black air behind them, be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning, then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once
pictures.name: pd_schendel_nacht

lines.text: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to speak first to His disciples: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.
I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!
Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.
But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.
And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.
Someone in the crowd said to Him, Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.
But Jesus replied, Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?
And He said to them, Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.
Then He told them a parable: The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.
So he thought to himself, What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?
Then he said, This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods.
Then I will say to myself, You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!
But God said to him, You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?
This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.
Then Jesus said to His disciples, Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.
Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?
Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!
And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.
For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.
Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.

Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.
Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.
But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
Lord, said Peter, are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?
And the Lord answered, Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.
Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But suppose that servant says in his heart, My master will be a long time in coming, and he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.
That servant who knows his master's will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.
But the one who unknowingly does things worthy of punishment will be beaten with few blows.
From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from him who has been entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.
I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.
They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.
Then Jesus said to the crowds, As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, A shower is coming, and that is what happens.
And when the south wind blows, you say, It will be hot, and it is.
You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don't you know how to interpret the present time?
And why don't you judge for yourselves what is right?

Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny.
